newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Torrid July for equities cools.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Torrid July for equities cools.

text.p: The torrid pace of equity options trading in July began to cool on Tuesday but traders said they expected action to pick up into the month end and the first few days of August.

"It's definitely a little bit slower than it was the last few weeks," said an equity options trader in Chicago. "But even on the slow days we're 15 to 20 percent better than we had been" on average earlier in the year.
Several traders said their firms were on track to post record options trading for the month of July and few doubted the trend would end.
"If the market gets into a range without the wild 100-point days it will definitely slow down, but I assume it will pick back up after that," the trader in Chicago said.

The heavy pace of equity options in July has been led mainly by action in technology stock options and the trend continued Tuesday, with Microsoft Corp, Dell Computer Corp, International Business Machines Corp and Intel Corp continuing to dominate most actives lists at the four options exchanges.
"As far as retail flow, it's all in equities and mostly in high techs," said an options trader on the East Coast.
In addition to the most popular technology names, others with busy options included Ascend Communications Inc, which had active calls as the stock rallied sharply.
In late trade, Ascend was up 5-1/2 at 52-1/8 on more than 21.5 million shares.
Among the options, the August 50 calls were the most active, with total volume of 4,265 contracts. The September 55 call traded 3,640 and the August 55 call traded nearly 1,700.
A few Cyrix Corp options were active as the stock rallied on news the company would merge with National Semiconductor Corp. Cyrix was up 1-13/16 at 24-7/8 after climbing as high as 26-1/8 intraday.
The Cyrix August 20 calls traded nearly 2,800 contracts, the August 25 calls traded nearly 2,200 and the August 20 puts traded more than 1,400.
The options trader in Chicago said he had a customer covering some Cyrix positions, buying back both puts and calls, but not in any large size.
In other trading, several Chase Manhattan Corp options were active, led by the August 110 call, which traded about 3,590 contracts.
The Chase August 100 call traded 1,480 and the August 105 put traded 1,635.
